what.text: Ashwagandha is a shrub, Withania somnifera, in the nightshade family, used in India's Ayurvedic medicine. Its root contains steroid-like compounds called withanolides, and alkaloids.

research.text: Human trials of ashwagandha are mostly small and short. They measured stress scores, cortisol and hormone levels. Several case series describe liver injury. Each study is listed as it was run.

research.title: Adults with chronic stress (Indian J Psychol Med 2012)

facts.v: Chandrasekhar K, Kapoor J, Anishetty S. Indian J Psychol Med 2012;34(3):255-62
single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
64 adults with a history of chronic stress
300 mg root extract capsule or placebo, twice a day
60 days
stress questionnaires; serum cortisol

research.found: Stress scores on all scales fell more on ashwagandha than on placebo (P<0.0001), and serum cortisol fell more (P=0.0006). Side effects were mild and similar in both groups.

src.label: Chandrasekhar et al., Indian J Psychol Med, PubMed

research.title: Stressed healthy adults (Medicine 2019)

facts.v: Lopresti AL, Smith SJ, Malvi H, Kodgule R. Medicine (Baltimore) 2019;98(37):e17186
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (CTRI/2017/08/009449)
60 adults with self-reported high stress
240 mg of a standardized extract or placebo, once a day
60 days
Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, DASS-21; cortisol, DHEA-S and testosterone

research.found: Anxiety scores (HAM-A) fell more on ashwagandha (P=.040); the DASS-21 difference was not significant (P=.096). Morning cortisol and DHEA-S fell more. Testosterone rose in men over time but not significantly more than on placebo (P=.158). No side effects were reported.

src.label: Lopresti et al., Medicine, PubMed

research.title: Aging, overweight men: hormones and vitality (Am J Mens Health 2019)

facts.v: Lopresti AL, Drummond PD, Smith SJ. Am J Mens Health 2019;13(2):1557988319835985
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover
57 overweight men aged 40 to 70 with mild fatigue; 43 completed both periods
an extract giving 21 mg of withanolide glycosides a day, or placebo
8 weeks per period, 16 weeks in all
fatigue and vigor (POMS-SF), Aging Males' Symptoms scale, saliva DHEA-S, testosterone, cortisol and estradiol

research.found: Saliva testosterone rose 14.7% more and DHEA-S 18% more on ashwagandha than on placebo. Fatigue, vigor, sexual well-being, cortisol and estradiol did not differ between groups.

src.label: Lopresti et al., Am J Mens Health, PubMed

research.title: Liver injury, 5 cases (Liver Int 2020)

facts.v: Björnsson HK, Björnsson ES, Avula B, et al. Liver Int 2020;40(4):825-829
case series; causality judged by the US Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network method
5 people (3 men), aged 21 to 62, 3 from Iceland and 2 from the US network
liver tests, symptoms, biopsy, chemical analysis of the supplements

research.found: All 5 developed jaundice 2 to 12 weeks after starting, with cholestatic or mixed liver injury and itching that lasted 5 to 20 weeks. None had liver failure. Liver tests returned to normal in 1 to 5 months in 4; 1 was lost to follow-up. Testing found ashwagandha and no other toxic compounds in the supplements.

src.label: Björnsson et al., Liver International, PubMed

research.title: Liver injury, 8 single-ingredient cases (Hepatol Commun 2023)

facts.v: Philips CA, Valsan A, Theruvath AH, et al. Hepatol Commun 2023;7(10):e0270
retrospective review of medical records at several Indian centers, 2019 to 2022
23 patients with liver injury linked to ashwagandha; 8 took a single-ingredient product and were reported in detail
liver tests, biopsy, outcomes, chemical analysis

research.found: Most were men, and cholestatic hepatitis was the most common pattern. 5 of the 8 had existing chronic liver disease; 3 developed acute-on-chronic liver failure and all 3 died. In the others, injury was prolonged but resolved. Tests found no adulteration.

src.label: Philips et al., Hepatology Communications, PubMed

research.text: A 2020 risk assessment by Denmark's DTU National Food Institute reviewed the evidence. It found that animal studies showed effects on sex hormones and reproduction in male rats, effects on thyroid hormones, and effects on the immune system. Reduced sperm quality and fertility were seen with plant parts other than the root. Some human trials and case reports suggested effects on the thyroid and sex hormones. It concluded no intake level of the root could be set as free of risk.

side.text: FDA does not review dietary supplements for safety before sale. The most serious reported harm is liver injury, sometimes severe and, in people with existing liver disease, fatal. A Danish risk assessment also raises concerns about sex hormones, reproduction and the thyroid.

items.text: case series from Iceland, the US and India describe jaundice and cholestatic hepatitis starting 2 to 12 weeks after use. Most cases resolved over months. In the Indian series, 3 people with existing chronic liver disease developed liver failure and died.

DTU added that most human hormone studies were in men who already had poor sperm quality and altered hormone levels.
